title: Aleppo Pine: Old Aleppo Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Its cones stay sealed for years and open in fire, so the blaze that kills the tree sows the next one. Five Aleppo pines mapped.
intro: An Aleppo pine keeps its cones locked shut on the branch for years and opens them with heat, so the fire that kills the tree sows the next generation of it. That trick is why a nineteenth century engineer bet a whole hillside on the species. When Nice became French in 1860 the slopes of Mont Boron were bare rock, and the replanting begun in 1862 is the pine forest you walk through today. The other four are city trees. Rome's grows in the Villa Celimontana, one of two officially monumental trees standing within a few metres of each other. Madrid's, about 150 years old, is in the Campo del Moro under the west front of the Royal Palace. Barcelona's, at about 122, is in the Torre Girona gardens, and Florence's stands on Via Giramondino. Five cities, all of them Mediterranean, which for this pine is simply home.
